site_or_subject: Johor Data Centre Development Coordination Committee approvals, rejections and Tier 1/2 halt
operator: Johor State Government (DCDCC; Special Technical Committee)
record: Johor's committee (formally the Jawatankuasa Pembangunan Pusat Data Negeri Johor, JPPDNJ, which screens applications for zoning, infrastructure, water, electricity and buffer zones before they reach local authorities, under a state data-centre planning guideline approved in April 2024) began vetting applications in June 2024 and, per its vice-chairman Lee Ting Han (Nov 2024, press), rejected nearly 30% of applications in five months (4 of 14 foreign-operator bids), citing failure to show sustainable water/energy practices and sites lacking utility infrastructure; Johor capacity was stated at 10 MW (2021), ~1.3 GW (Nov 2024), 2.7 GW projected 2027. In a 28 Nov 2024 state-assembly answer the Menteri Besar stated data centres must meet PUE not above 1.5 and WUE of 1.8; on 20 Nov 2025 exco Mohd Jafni Md Shukor told the assembly WUE must be below 1.8 under the planning guideline, with approval priority for applicants not using Syarikat Air Johor (SAJ) water. The state reported 42 approved projects (RM164.45bn) to Q2 2025 and, in a Nov 2025 written answer, 17 operating data centres. In Nov 2025 Jafni told the NST that 51 projects were approved (17 operational, 11 under construction, 23 unbuilt) and the state 'will no longer approve' Tier 1 and Tier 2 facilities, which can use up to 50 million litres/day versus ~200,000 L/day for Tier 3/4; data centres needing water must use reclaimed water rather than SAJ supply.

record: MOTIE's March 2023 plan to ease capital-area data-centre concentration counted 147 data centres with 1,762 MW of demand (Dec 2022) and projected 732 facilities with 49,397 MW of new demand by 2029, 58.2% (28,733 MW) in the capital area, where only 40 of 601 applications (6.7%) could be supplied on schedule versus 64 of 131 (48.9%) elsewhere. Asia Economy reports that the 11th Basic Plan for Electricity Supply and Demand projects data-centre consumption of 30 TWh and peak demand of 6.2 GW by 2038, and that KEPCO reported 117 applications totalling 7,343 MW as of Aug 2023, of which 76 (4,718 MW) could be supplied [press]. Kim Seong-won from MOTIE/KEPCO show 290 data-centre supply applications from Aug 2024 to Jun 2025, 195 (67%) in the Seoul metropolitan area requesting ~20 GW; of cases reaching MOTIE review, 4 of 19 metro applications passed (21%) versus 10 of 14 non-metro (71%). The assessment (introduced Aug 2024) covers facilities of 10 MW or more and is reviewed by the Power Policy Deliberation Committee; MOTIE's Aug 2024 release names supply headroom (25 points) and difficulty of securing headroom (20 points) among its items, while press reports the overall split as technical 60, non-technical 20, policy 20 points. MOTIE's March 2023 plan states that 60% of data-centre sites and 70% of data-centre power demand are in the capital area.

site_or_subject: NSW state-significant data-centre approvals and Sydney potable water use
operator: NSW Department of Planning; Sydney Water; AirTrunk, Amazon, Microsoft, Goodman (Road 1)
record: NSW Planning confirmed to Reuters (Sep 2025) that all 10 data-centre applications ruled on since 2021 were approved (A$6.6bn), projecting up to 9.6 GL/yr of potable water (~2% of Sydney's maximum supply); Reuters reported Sydney Water projecting data centres could use up to 135 GL (a quarter of available water) by 2035; Sydney Water's own answers to the NSW Legislative Council data-centres inquiry (received 22 Jun 2026) instead give 26 smaller data centres approved and connected, 101 servicing requests (75 larger facilities totalling ~250 ML/day), seven planning agreements for 74 ML/day, and average-day demand of ~110 ML/day by 2030 and ~260 ML/day by 2035 if all requests proceed, against ~1,500 ML/day supplied across Greater Sydney (about 95 GL/yr, roughly 17%), attributing the 15-25% range to other submissions citing Sydney Water. Site figures in planning documents: AirTrunk 320 MW (rainwater cuts potable use 0.4%); two Amazon centres 195.2 MW and up to 92 ML/yr. NSW's only water standard is that the government be 'satisfied that the development contains measures designed to minimise the consumption of potable water'. The NSW Planning Portal lists Road 1 Data Centre (SSD-80814238, Macquarie Park, 34.3 MW) as approved 1 Oct 2026 with a Sydney Water Growth Data Form attached but no public water volume.
